title: Replace monolithic aggregation middleware with streaming coalescer and modernize runtime deps
creator: Priya Patel
description: Background: The existing backend aggregator is a large synchronous middleware that performs heavy fan-out, field merging, and ad-hoc caching. Over time it has accumulated special-case code paths, a fragile LRU wrapper, and several transitive dependency versions pinned for legacy reasons. Symptom: high p95 tail latency for console API routes that aggregate multiple downstream services, frequent GC pressure under load, and occasional hot locks on the in-memory cache causing request stalls. Goal: Replace the monolithic aggregator with a composable streaming coalescer that performs continuous batching and KV- prefix caching, while upgrading the Node runtime and critical dependencies (GraphQL server, LRU cache lib, TypeScript) to reduce CPU overhead, improve memory behaviour, and remove contention points. This ticket covers design, a proof-of-concept, implementation, and staged rollout with metrics gating.
acceptance_criteria: p95 reduction of aggregation-heavy console routes by >= 30% in the staging load test compared to baseline
End-to-end error rate for targeted routes does not increase beyond 0.5% during canary
Aggregate memory footprint per replica reduced by >= 15% under representative workload
No production-only feature regressions; GraphQL shape and auth headers preserved
Dependencies upgraded: Node 20.x -> 22.x, graphql v16 -> v17, lru-cache -> quick-ttl or equivalent, TypeScript -> 5.x (compiles clean)
Automated benchmark script and dashboards linked in ticket
implementation_steps: Design streaming coalescer API: request grouping key, max latency threshold, batch size, and KV prefix cache contract
Build POC as a lightweight middleware that can be enabled via feature flag on a subset of routes (metrics-only mode)
Add server-side dataloader-like batching for GraphQL resolvers that map to the same downstream endpoint
Replace hotlock-protected LRU with sharded TTL cache (quick-ttl or in-house) and observe lock-free reads
Upgrade runtime and deps in a separate branch; fix type errors and deprecation warnings
Run synthetic load tests comparing old aggregator vs coalescer (token-level, payload sizes, biz-graphs)
Create migration plan and feature flag with phased rollout (10% -> 50% -> 100%) with automatic rollback on SLO regression
Clean up legacy aggregator code paths and remove deprecated configuration flags after 2 successful releases
risk_mitigation: Feature-flagged rollout with traffic-slicing by tenant to minimize blast radius
Maintain a hot path fallback that routes to legacy aggregator if coalescer errors exceed threshold
Preserve request/response contract and headers; add schema-level regression checks in CI
Monitor GC and allocated heap; pre-deploy Node GC tuning if needed
test_plan: Unit tests for coalescer grouping logic, TTL cache eviction and concurrency invariants
Integration tests that verify GraphQL resolver batching correctness against mock downstreams
Load tests simulating 3 representative tenant workloads (single-tenant, multi-tenant, bursty)
Canary metrics: p95 latency, errors, cpu, heap, goroutine count-equivalent (node event loop stats)
rollback_plan: Immediate feature flag disable to revert traffic to legacy aggregator
If severe regressions detected, revert dependency upgrade PR and redeploy previous image
Post-mortem and follow-up revert checklist if customer-facing incidents occur
